# Draft:Harsha Wijayawardhana

Harsha Wijayawardhana, FBCS, CITP  is a Sri Lankan technologist, early contributor to Internet development in Sri Lanka, researcher, and Chartered ICT professional, Known for his contributions to the digitization of the Sinhala and Tamil languages, Unicode standardization, Internationalized Domain Names (IDNs), Universal Acceptance (UA), and the broader development of Sri Lanka's digital infrastructure. He is a Fellow of the British Computer Society (FBCS) and Chartered IT Professional (CITP), and has advocated for multilingual Internet access in South Asia. Wijayawardhana is also known for his research on Sinhala numerals, the "Sinhala Zero," Brahmi-derived numeral evolution, and the digital preservation of Sri Lankan heritage.
Early Life and Education
Harsha Wijayawardhana received his early education at Ananda College, Colombo, and later attended the German Swiss International School (GSIS) in Hong Kong. He completed his higher education in the United States, graduating from the University of Miami, Florida.
Career
Early Internet and E-Governance Work (1996–2002)
From 1996 to 2002, Wijayawardhana contributed significantly to the development of Internet infrastructure and e-Governance in Sri Lanka. He became a key member of the team that produced weekly radio programs titled "Internet Sampath Bavithaya" (Use of Internet Resources) in both Sinhala and English on the Sri Lanka Broadcasting Corporation (SLBC). The Sinhala program commenced in 1997 and continued until 2016, making it one of the longest-running programs on Swadeshiya Sevaya.
As webmaster of www.lk, he became a key member of the Internet Committee of the Council for Information Technology (CINTEC), where the first work on Sinhala Unicode implementation began. In 1998, he served as network designer for the UNESCO-funded Kotmale Community Radio Internet Project, which became the first multi-purpose Telecentre in the world and the first site to use dynamic routing in Sri Lanka.
He designed and implemented government networks including the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Information Department of Sri Lanka, and the Policy Research and Information Unit (PRIU) of the Presidential Secretariat. He was also responsible for setting up the Software Development Unit (SDU) of the University of Colombo School of Computing (UCSC).
Unicode and Sinhala Language Computing
From 2002 onwards, Wijayawardhana became an advocate of Sinhala Unicode technology. He developed Sinhala Unicode-compliant fonts in his laboratory and became a member of the Local Language Working Group (LLWG) of the Information and Communication Technology Agency (ICTA) of Sri Lanka.
He was a member of the committee involved in the standardization of Sinhala SLS 1134 and carried out the third revision of SLS 1134. He led a team of scholars researching numeration in the Sinhala language and published results at the National Symposium in Archaeology. Through his work, he identified several sets of numerations in Sinhala, and two sets of numerals - Sinhala Illakkam and Lith Illakkam - were encoded in Unicode in 2010 and included in Sri Lanka Standard SLS 1134:2011.
He represented Sri Lanka at Working Group 2 (WG2) of ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 2 several times, where he advocated for the encoding of Sinhala numerals in Unicode. He is a member of the Information Technology Sectoral Committee of the Sri Lanka Standards Institution (SLSI).
Wijayawardhana has written extensively on Unicode implementation and Sinhala computing for the Daily FT, contributing articles on topics including Sinhala and Tamil digital device issues, Unicode font implementation, and the evolution of the Sinhala script.
Internationalized Domain Names (IDN)
Wijayawardhana played a role in the establishment of Sri Lanka's Internationalized Domain Names (IDNs). In 2010, Sri Lanka applied through ICANN's IDN Fast Track process for .ලංකා (Lanka in Sinhala) and .இலங்கை (Ilangai in Tamil). These domains were approved by the ICANN Board on 5 August 2010, and formally delegated to the LK Domain Registry.
In December 2017, ICANN and local experts convened in Colombo to launch the Sinhala Generation Panel (GP), tasked with developing Root Zone Label Generation Rules (LGR) for the Sinhala script. Wijayawardhana serves as Co-Chair of the Sinhala Generation Panel alongside Dr. Ruvan Weerasinghe. The Sinhala GP completed its work on LGR in 2020, establishing rules for forming valid top-level domain names in Sinhala script.
ICANN and International Policy Work
Wijayawardhana has been an active participant in ICANN's At-Large community and the Asia Pacific Regional At-Large Organization (APRALO) since the mid-2010s. He has contributed to ICANN working groups focused on internationalized domain names and multilingual Internet policy, including:
* Latin Script Generation Panel: Contributing to discussions on diacritic variant policy development
* IDN Variant TLD Implementation Guidelines: Participating in working group activities related to variant management rules
* Universal Acceptance (UA) Advocacy: Leading initiatives in Sri Lanka to promote Universal Acceptance, a key requirement for a truly multilingual Internet
He chairs the Local Language Working Group (LLWG) of ICTA and has organized numerous workshops on Universal Acceptance, Email Address Internationalization (EAI), and DNS security for various government agencies and private sector organizations in Sri Lanka.
Cybersecurity and Digital Literacy
Wijayawardhana has been an advocate for cybersecurity awareness and digital literacy in Sri Lanka. In 2018, he was quoted by The Sunday Times discussing the proliferation of false profiles on social media platforms and the security risks they pose, speaking in his capacity at the University of Colombo.
Leadership and Organizational Roles
Wijayawardhana has held numerous leadership positions in Sri Lankan ICT development:
* Board Member of the LK Domain Registry (nic.lk) since its inception
* Board Member, Bank of Ceylon (2018–present)
* Board Member of Lanka Government Information Infrastructure (LGII) from 2010 to 2015
* One of seven founding members of the Lanka Educational Research Network (LEARN)
* ICT Consultant to the Telecommunication Regulatory Commission of Sri Lanka (2014)
* ICT Consultant to H.E. the President of Sri Lanka (2010–2015)
* Chief Operating Officer (COO) / Chief Technology Officer (CTO) of Theekshana R&D since its inception in 2006
* Founding President of the Internet Society Sri Lanka Chapter (ISOC-LK)
Major Projects
Wijayawardhana led or contributed to several national ICT projects:
* The Automated Fingerprint Identification System (AFIS) for the Sri Lanka Police, an e-Governance project implemented in Sri Lanka.
* Birth, Marriage, and Death Certificates Issuance System deployed throughout Sri Lanka
* Householder List Database containing individual data on every Sri Lankan, set up at every Divisional Secretariat
* Electronic Government Procurement (eGP) System of the Government of Sri Lanka (2017–2019), developed under a World Bank grant. The system became fully operational in May 2019 and is now used by hundreds of government organizations and vendors
Research and Publications
Wijayawardhana authored the book "Numeration in the Sinhala Language" based on extensive research into historical Sinhala numeral systems used before 1815. The book explores the evolution of Sinhala Illakkam, its multiplicative-additive structure, and the Sinhala zero. His research draws on epigraphic evidence from ancient inscriptions documented by scholars such as Senerat Paranavitana and D.M. de Z. Wickremasinghe.
He has published several scientific papers on Unicode, Sinhala computing, and Internet governance, and maintains the website www.fonts.lk, one of the first websites dedicated to Sinhala and Tamil Unicode implementation (developed 2004–2005).
Recognition and Awards
* Fellow of the British Computer Society (FBCS): Recognized for his contributions to ICT development.
* Chartered IT Professional (CITP): Professional designation from BCS
* Involved in early Internet initiatives in Sri Lanka: Recognized in 2015 by ISOC, LK Domain Registry, and ICTA at the celebration of 20 years of connecting Sri Lanka to commercial Internet
* ICT History Profile''': Featured on ICT-History.lk for his contributions to Sri Lankan ICT development
